observed_prior_facts: whether a measurement run started and has not yet completed, and the brief's content hash at run start — a mid-run edit is only a violation relative to that prior state
reason: An edit to the brief is not a violation per se (editing plus re-measuring is allowed); compliance is decided only by the sequence — did the edit land between batches of an in-progress measured run.

artifact: the working tree at commit time (git status --porcelain output)
pattern: a line beginning with `??` whose path matches a test-file pattern (e.g. tests/** or *spec*/*test* file) at the moment of commit
reason: An untracked test file is a purely structural fact of the repository at commit time; its presence decides non-compliance with no reading of intent.

Deciding compliance means judging whether a claim's strength ('absence guaranteed', 'index healthy') is actually licensed by the kind of evidence behind it (sampling vs. a real query) — an assessment of the meaning of the claim relative to its evidence, not a textual pattern.

artifact: the edited spec file path together with the approval register (מרשם)
pattern: on an Edit/Write to docs/superpowers/specs/**, the presence of that spec's path listed as approved in the register decides whether the edit passes without a brainstorming session; absence blocks
reason: The rule reduces to a lookup: an approved-in-register spec licenses editing itself, an unlisted/new spec does not — presence or absence of a register entry is decisive without reading intent.

Deciding whether a test asserts more than honest data can satisfy requires evaluating the meaning of its assertion against what the data domain makes possible (distinctive vs. incidental identifiers) — a quality/semantics judgement, not a nameable textual pattern.
